problem: Owners plan preconstructed-deck purchases in spreadsheets because the product only tracks single boosters, so precon prices and stock are never compared with the sealed products they replace.
outcome: An owner tracks preconstructed decks beside boosters, with the same price history, alerts and availability view.
intended_user_value: The owner sees one comparable view of sealed product value instead of maintaining a parallel spreadsheet.
scope: Model preconstructed decks as a first-class sealed product type.
Ingest precon listings from the existing supported retailers.
Extend price history, alerts and availability to precons.
requirements: A precon is stored with set, product code, release date and retailer listings.
Price history records precon prices on the existing collection schedule.
Alerts support precons using the existing threshold rules.
Search and availability views filter by sealed product type.
acceptance_criteria: A precon can be created, listed and opened with its retailer listings.
Precon price history is recorded and rendered on the existing chart.
An alert on a precon fires under the existing threshold rules.
Search filters results by sealed product type.
Existing booster behaviour is unchanged by the new product type.
constraints: Reuse the existing ingestion schedule; no additional recurring provider cost.
risks: Retailer precon listings may not expose a stable product code.
Product-type modelling may force a migration of existing booster rows.

adr_disposition.reason: Implements the existing product-data ownership decision without changing it.

owner_decisions: Precons reuse the booster ingestion schedule rather than a new collector.
Deck-contents analysis is deferred out of this work item.

source.summary: Owner asked for precon support; scope agreed as sealed product parity, excluding card-level analysis.
